cohort: Singleton pregnant patients admitted for threatened preterm labor with a cervical length < 25 mm.
finding: Cervical pessary placement significantly reduced the rates of preterm birth (<37, <34, and <32 weeks) and adverse neonatal outcomes after an episode of arrested preterm labor, particularly when the onset of symptoms was before 30 gestational weeks.
gest_age: Targeted outcomes for birth before < 37 weeks, < 34 weeks, and < 32 weeks; relevant for patients with symptom onset before 30 gestational weeks or gestational age at first admission > 30.1 gestational weeks.
